title: Learn, test, and extend the Synthia generative mesh
objective: Use the supplied books, user instructions, Klein tools, ATO materials, Human Design repositories, and GitHub research to build a shared generative mesh whose tools learn from one another while preserving distinct functions.
instructions: Treat the user's stated correspondences as instructions with provenance, not as universal facts unless sources independently support them.
AUTOLING reads, normalizes, learns language, and shares learned language with the mesh.
Control of Grammar learns grammatical constraints and controls expression without replacing meaning.
DISEMINER extracts candidate semantic triples and implied relationships.
ATO maps supported semantic triples to recoverable binary transformations.
The Paraphraser changes surface expression while preserving the supported relation graph.
AutoNovel writes actual explanations, stories, and reports rather than outlines alone.
The Symbolic Validator checks generated claims and modules against source evidence.
A gate-line is a possibility for emergence; emergence activates only when a channel is completed.
Keep Planetary, Dimension, Gate, Line, Color, Tone, Base, Degree, Minute, Second, Arc, Zodiac, and House as addressable coordinates.
Keep Degree-Color, Minute-Tone, and Second-Base as instructed proportional pairings.
Do not equate Zodiac or House with Color or Tone unless repeatable evidence establishes the mapping.
Every generated tool is a composable input-transform-output triplet with an ATO genome, provenance, tests, and rollback history.
Generated changes remain proposals until their acceptance tests pass.
acceptanceTests: All registered Klein organs receive accepted mesh learning after reload.
New language learned by AUTOLING is visible to the other organs through shared mesh state.
Every accepted relation resolves to source ID, location, checksum, and original text.
Generated reports contain prose and claim-level evidence.
Corrections propagate without deleting prior revisions.
Generated modules remain inactive until automated tests pass.
A full shutdown and restart preserves accepted learning and tool growth.
